quick: Oral: start 5 mg once daily; usual 10-40 mg/day; max 100 mg/day
May be taken without regard to food
Use only if clearly needed; limited data
Excreted in milk; weigh benefit vs risk

summary: Oral minoxidil is a potent direct arteriolar vasodilator reserved for severe symptomatic hypertension or hypertension with target organ damage not controlled by a diuretic plus two other antihypertensives. It causes reflex tachycardia and marked fluid retention, so it is given with a beta-blocker and a diuretic. It carries a boxed warning for pericardial effusion (possibly tamponade) and possible angina exacerbation. (Topical minoxidil is a separate product used for hair loss.)
indications: Severe symptomatic hypertension, or hypertension associated with target organ damage, not manageable with a diuretic plus two other antihypertensive drugs

dosage.d: Initial 5 mg once daily; titrate to 10, 20, then 40 mg in single or divided doses
dosage.n: Effective range usually 10-40 mg/day; maximum 100 mg/day

dosage.d: Initial 0.2 mg/kg once daily; increase by 50-100% increments
Once daily if supine diastolic reduced <30 mmHg; divide into two doses if reduced >30 mmHg
dosage.n: Adjust no more often than every 3 days

dosage.d: Give with a beta-blocker (or other sympatholytic) and a diuretic
dosage.n: To control reflex tachycardia and fluid retention

admin: Almost always co-administer a beta-blocker to prevent reflex tachycardia and a loop diuretic to control fluid retention
Titrate slowly, no more often than every 3 days
Monitor body weight and signs of fluid overload
Counsel on hypertrichosis (excess body hair) with chronic use
moa: Minoxidil sulfate (active metabolite) opens ATP-sensitive potassium channels in vascular smooth muscle, hyperpolarizing the cell and producing direct arteriolar (not venous) vasodilation. The fall in peripheral resistance triggers baroreceptor-mediated reflex tachycardia and renal sodium/water retention, necessitating combination therapy.

absolute: Pheochromocytoma (may stimulate catecholamine release from the tumor)
Known hypersensitivity to minoxidil or formulation components
relative: Recent myocardial infarction or significant coronary disease (angina risk)
Pulmonary hypertension associated with mitral stenosis
monitor: Fluid retention and worsening heart failure

preg: Limited human data. Use only if the potential benefit justifies the risk; neonatal hypertrichosis has been reported with maternal use.
lact: Minoxidil is excreted in human milk; weigh benefit of breastfeeding against potential infant exposure.
renal: Reduced clearance in renal impairment; lower doses or reduced frequency may be required, and dialysis removes the drug.
hepatic: Use with caution in hepatic impairment.

major: Guanethidine (profound orthostatic hypotension; discontinue guanethidine first or hospitalize)
moderate: NSAIDs (may blunt antihypertensive effect and worsen fluid retention)
Diuretics required to offset sodium/water retention
interactions.food: May be taken without regard to meals.
interactions.diagnostics: May alter ECG (T-wave changes), generally reversible.

monitoring: Body weight and signs of fluid retention
Echocardiography/ECG for pericardial effusion if suspected
counsel: Increased and darkened body/face hair is common and usually reverses after stopping
Do not stop suddenly; rebound hypertension can occur
Report rapid weight gain, swelling, breathlessness, or chest pain promptly
Take the prescribed beta-blocker and diuretic as directed
This is the oral antihypertensive tablet, distinct from topical minoxidil for hair loss
pk: Up to 75 hours of antihypertensive effect
pearls: Reserved for severe/resistant hypertension; not for mild cases
Always combine with a beta-blocker and a diuretic
Antihypertensive effect persists well beyond the plasma half-life
Hypertrichosis led to development of topical minoxidil for hair loss
missed: Take the missed dose when remembered; if near the next dose, skip it. Do not double up. Maintain regular dosing to avoid rebound hypertension.
overdose: Excessive hypotension is the main concern, with reflex tachycardia. Treat with IV normal saline; if a vasopressor is needed, phenylephrine, dopamine, or norepinephrine is preferred (avoid epinephrine/isoproterenol which add tachycardia). Minoxidil is dialyzable.
